cohort: 470 bacterial isolates from women with puerperal infections in Bangladesh
finding: The most common bacterial species isolated were Escherichia coli, Enterococcus faecalis, Staphylococcus haemolyticus, Proteus mirabilis, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Enterobacter cloacae, with varying resistance profiles and genetic characteristics, including the presence of specific resistance genes like blaCTX-M-15, blaNDM-1, and blaNDM-7.
mod_finding: S. aureus and Acinetobacter baumannii were isolated at a higher frequency from wound infections after cesarean section.
